root.name: Bird Opening: Lasker Variation
root.moves: 1. f4 d5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. e3 c5

overview: In this reversed-Dutch Bird, Black plays 3...c5 against 3.e3 in the style of the Queen's Gambit. White usually plays 4.b3 Nc6 5.Bb2 e6 and develops with Be2, O-O and d3 or Ne5, with the f4 pawn controlling e5. Black fights for the centre and the dark squares are the battleground.

white_ideas.idea: Play b3 and Bb2 to put pressure on the long diagonal
Control e5 with the f4 pawn and a knight, then castle
Play Be2, O-O and d3 or Ne5 and keep a flexible set-up

black_ideas.idea: Play ...Nc6, ...e6 and ...Be7 and fight for the centre with ...c4 or ...e5
Pin the knight with ...Bg4 or hit the centre with ...c4
Exploit the weakened e1-h4 diagonal with ...Qb6

typical_structures.structure: Reversed Dutch with White f4/e3 pawns against Black c5/d5
Black c5/d5/e6 centre against a White fianchetto bishop on b2

character.notes: Positional play with both sides developing to good squares; the f4 pawn gives some tactical risk but not much.

structure.notes: Pawn tension in the centre with c5 and d5 against f4 and e3: flexible.

approach.notes: A respected opening used by strong players, though uncommon: standard.

level.notes: Plans are clear but the f4 weakening needs care.

character.reason: Positional play with some kingside risk but no forcing lines.

structure.reason: The centre is in tension with pawns on c5, d5, e3 and f4.

plans.reason: White plays b3 and Bb2 and controls e5.
